steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a paper on HumanGaussian, our framework for text-driven 3D human generation using Gaussian Splatting. Cover prior approaches and their trade-offs, the challenges of applying Gaussian Splatting here, our two main technical ideas, and a list of contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Text-driven 3D human generation: applications and earlier approaches
- Body-prior methods and the efficiency/quality trade-off
- 3D Gaussian Splatting and its two challenges for humans
- HumanGaussian: Structure-Aware SDS and Annealed Negative Prompt Guidance
- Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Background
  - 3D humans from user condition: virtual try-on (cite), immersive telepresence (cite)
  - text-driven 3D human generation: appearance + geometry from text
  - traditional: regress from multi-view captures, then manual rigging/skinning (cite)
  - DreamFusion (cite): score distillation sampling (SDS), 2D text-to-image prior (Stable Diffusion (cite), Imagen (cite))
  - fine on single objects (cite), hard for articulated human bodies

- Body priors
  - SDS + body shape models SMPL (cite), imGHUM (cite)
  - human priors in mesh / NeRF: shape as mesh/density initialization (cite), or LBS deformation field (cite)
  - trade-off: mesh-based (cite) miss accessories, wrinkles; NeRF-based (cite) time/memory heavy at high resolution
  - fine-grained + efficient = unsolved

- 3DGS
  - 3D Gaussian Splatting (cite): explicit, real-time reconstruction; multi-scale, suits humans
  - challenge 1: tile-based rasterization, sorting and \alpha -blending splats per view frustum -> few high-confidence Gaussians get gradients; sparse gradient hinders optimization (cite); need structural guidance for humans
  - challenge 2: naive SDS needs large CFG (cite) scale (e.g. 100 (cite)) -> over-saturation; stochastic SDS makes gradient-based density control unstable -> blur, floating artifacts

- HumanGaussian
  - efficient yet effective; fine-grained geometry, realistic appearance
  - intuition: 3DGS periodic Gaussian shrinkage/growing; density control guided by human structure
  - key: explicit structural guidance + gradient regularization
  - Structure-Aware SDS: generic priors in previous work (cite) like SfM points or Point-E (cite) vs anchoring Gaussians on SMPL-X mesh; densification/pruning near body surface
  - extend Stable Diffusion (cite) to denoise RGB and depth jointly; dual-branch, joint distribution
  - Annealed Negative Prompt Guidance: generative score + classifier score; decreasing negative prompt guidance; nominal CFG (e.g. 7.5), also shown concurrently (cite)
  - high SDS variance -> blurry geometry with gradient-based density control (cite); prune by Gaussian size in prune-only phase

- Contributions
  - HumanGaussian framework; one of earliest Gaussian Splatting attempts for text-driven 3D humans
  - Structure-Aware SDS
  - Annealed Negative Prompt Guidance
  - experiments: superior efficiency, competitive quality

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Creating high-quality 3D humans from a user condition is very important for many applications, from virtual try-on to immersive telepresence. For this, researchers study the task of text-driven 3D human generation, which synthesizes the appearance and geometry of a character from text prompts. Traditional methods use a hand-crafted pipeline: 3D models are first regressed from multi-view human captures, and then they go through a series of manual processes such as rigging and skinning. To reduce the human labor of creating 3D assets with diverse layouts, the exemplar work DreamFusion proposes score distillation sampling (SDS), which uses the rich 2D text-to-image prior (e.g., Stable Diffusion, Imagen) by optimizing 3D scenes so that they render samples lying on the manifold of higher likelihood. These methods get reasonable results on single objects, but it is hard for them to model detailed human bodies with complex articulations.

To add structural guidance, recent text-driven 3D human works combine SDS with body shape models like SMPL and imGHUM. A common paradigm is to put human priors into representations such as mesh and neural radiance field (NeRF), either by using the body shape as mesh/density initialization, or by learning a deformation field based on linear blend skinning (LBS). But most of them have to trade off between efficiency and quality. The mesh-based methods have trouble modeling fine topologies like accessories and wrinkles, and the NeRF-based methods take a lot of time and memory to render high-resolution results. So it is still an unsolved problem how to do fine-grained generation efficiently.

- 3DGS
  - 3D Gaussian Splatting (cite): explicit, real-time reconstruction; multi-scale, suits humans
  - challenge 1: tile-based rasterization, sorting and \alpha -blending splats per view frustum -> few high-confidence Gaussians get gradients; sparse gradient hinders optimization (cite); need structural guidance for humans
  - challenge 2: naive SDS needs large CFG (cite) scale (e.g. 100 (cite)) -> over-saturation; stochastic SDS makes gradient-based density control unstable -> blur, floating artifacts

- HumanGaussian
  - efficient yet effective; fine-grained geometry, realistic appearance
  - intuition: 3DGS periodic Gaussian shrinkage/growing; density control guided by human structure
  - key: explicit structural guidance + gradient regularization
  - Structure-Aware SDS: generic priors in previous work (cite) like SfM points or Point-E (cite) vs anchoring Gaussians on SMPL-X mesh; densification/pruning near body surface
  - extend Stable Diffusion (cite) to denoise RGB and depth jointly; dual-branch, joint distribution
  - Annealed Negative Prompt Guidance: generative score + classifier score; decreasing negative prompt guidance; nominal CFG (e.g. 7.5), also shown concurrently (cite)
  - high SDS variance -> blurry geometry with gradient-based density control (cite); prune by Gaussian size in prune-only phase

- Contributions
  - HumanGaussian framework; one of earliest Gaussian Splatting attempts for text-driven 3D humans
  - Structure-Aware SDS
  - Annealed Negative Prompt Guidance
  - experiments: superior efficiency, competitive quality

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Creating high-quality 3D humans from a user condition is very important for many applications, from virtual try-on to immersive telepresence. For this, researchers study the task of text-driven 3D human generation, which synthesizes the appearance and geometry of a character from text prompts. Traditional methods use a hand-crafted pipeline: 3D models are first regressed from multi-view human captures, and then they go through a series of manual processes such as rigging and skinning. To reduce the human labor of creating 3D assets with diverse layouts, the exemplar work DreamFusion proposes score distillation sampling (SDS), which uses the rich 2D text-to-image prior (e.g., Stable Diffusion, Imagen) by optimizing 3D scenes so that they render samples lying on the manifold of higher likelihood. These methods get reasonable results on single objects, but it is hard for them to model detailed human bodies with complex articulations.

To add structural guidance, recent text-driven 3D human works combine SDS with body shape models like SMPL and imGHUM. A common paradigm is to put human priors into representations such as mesh and neural radiance field (NeRF), either by using the body shape as mesh/density initialization, or by learning a deformation field based on linear blend skinning (LBS). But most of them have to trade off between efficiency and quality. The mesh-based methods have trouble modeling fine topologies like accessories and wrinkles, and the NeRF-based methods take a lot of time and memory to render high-resolution results. So it is still an unsolved problem how to do fine-grained generation efficiently.

Recently, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), an explicit neural representation, gives a new perspective for real-time scene reconstruction. It allows multi-scale modeling across multiple granularities, and this suits 3D human generation. However, using this representation for the task is non-trivial, and there are two challenges. 1) 3DGS does a tile-based rasterization by sorting and \alpha -blending anisotropic splats in each view frustum, and only a small set of high-confidence Gaussians get back-propagated. But as shown in 3D surface-/volume-rendering studies, sparse gradient can hinder the network optimization of geometry and appearance. So 3DGS needs structural guidance, especially in the human domain, which needs hierarchical structure modeling and controllable generation. 2) Naive SDS needs a large classifier-free guidance (CFG) scale to align image and text (e.g., 100, as in DreamFusion). But this hurts visual quality with over-saturated patterns, which makes realistic human generation difficult. Also, because the SDS loss is stochastic, the original gradient-based density control in 3DGS is unstable and gives blurry results with floating artifacts.

In this paper we propose HumanGaussian, an efficient yet effective framework that generates high-quality 3D humans with fine-grained geometry and realistic appearance. Our intuition is that 3D Gaussian Splatting is an efficient renderer with periodic Gaussian shrinkage or growing, and this adaptive density control can naturally be guided by intrinsic human structures. The key is to add explicit structural guidance and gradient regularization to help the Gaussian optimization. Specifically, we first propose a Structure-Aware SDS that learns human appearance and geometry jointly. Previous studies use generic priors like Structure-from-Motion (SfM) points or Point-E, but we instead anchor the initial positions of the Gaussians on the SMPL-X mesh. Because of this, the densification and pruning processes that follow focus on the regions around the body surface, and they capture geometric deformations like accessories and wrinkles effectively. We also extend the pre-trained Stable Diffusion so that it denoises the image RGB and depth at the same time, and use it as our SDS source model. This dual-branch design distills the joint distribution of two spatially-aligned targets (i.e., RGB and depth), which helps the Gaussians converge with both structural guidance and textural realism. To make the renderings look more natural, we design an Annealed Negative Prompt Guidance. We decompose SDS into a noisier generative score and a cleaner classifier score, and we give the latter a decreasing negative prompt guidance, which allows realistic generation under nominal CFG scales (e.g., 7.5); concurrent text-to-3D studies have also shown this. This way we avoid over-saturated patterns by using appropriate CFG scales that balance sample quality and diversity well. Moreover, because the SDS loss has high variance, using gradient information directly to control densities gives blurry geometry. Instead, we propose to remove floating artifacts based on Gaussian size in a prune-only phase.

To summarize, we have three main contributions: 1) We propose HumanGaussian, an efficient yet effective framework for high-quality 3D human generation with fine-grained geometry and realistic appearance. It is one of the earliest attempts at using Gaussian Splatting for the text-driven 3D human domain, and we hope it paves the way for future research. 2) We propose the Structure-Aware SDS, which jointly learns human appearance and geometry with explicit structural guidance. 3) We design the Annealed Negative Prompt Guidance to get realistic results and remove floating artifacts. Extensive experiments show that our framework has superior efficiency and competitive quality, and it renders vivid 3D humans in diverse scenarios.

steps.text:
Creating high-quality 3D humans from user conditions is of great importance to a wide variety of applications, ranging from virtual try-on [1,2,3,4] to immersive telepresence [5,6,7,8,9,10]. To this end, researchers explore text-driven 3D human generation, which synthesizes a character's appearance and geometry from text prompts. Traditional methods rely on a hand-crafted pipeline, in which 3D models are first regressed from multi-view human captures and then go through a series of manual processes such as rigging and skinning [11,12,13,14]. To reduce the human labor of creating 3D assets with diverse layouts, the exemplar work DreamFusion [15] proposes score distillation sampling (SDS), which harnesses rich 2D text-to-image priors (e.g., Stable Diffusion [16], Imagen [17]) by optimizing 3D scenes to render samples on the manifold of higher likelihood. Although these methods achieve reasonable results on single objects [18,19,20,21], they struggle to model detailed human bodies with complex articulations.

To incorporate structural guidance, recent text-driven 3D human studies combine SDS with body shape models such as SMPL [22] and imGHUM [23]. A common paradigm is to integrate human priors into representations like mesh and neural radiance field (NeRF), either by using the body shape as mesh/density initialization [24,25,26] or by learning a deformation field based on linear blend skinning (LBS) [27,28,29]. However, most of them trade off efficiency against quality: mesh-based methods [30,31,32] struggle to model fine topologies like accessories and wrinkles, while NeRF-based methods [33,34,35] are time- and memory-consuming when rendering high-resolution results. Achieving fine-grained generation efficiently thus remains an unsolved problem.

Recently, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) [36], an explicit neural representation, has offered a new perspective for real-time scene reconstruction. It enables multi-scale modeling across multiple granularities, which suits 3D human generation. Nevertheless, exploiting this representation for the task is non-trivial, with two challenges: 1) 3DGS performs tile-based rasterization by sorting and \alpha -blending anisotropic splats within each view frustum, which back-propagates only a small set of high-confidence Gaussians. As verified in 3D surface-/volume-rendering studies [37,38,39,40], such sparse gradients can hinder network optimization of geometry and appearance. Structural guidance is therefore required in 3DGS, especially in the human domain, which demands hierarchical structure modeling and generation controllability. 2) Naive SDS requires a large classifier-free guidance (CFG) [41] scale for image-text alignment (e.g., 100 as used in [15]), but this sacrifices visual quality with over-saturated patterns and makes realistic human generation difficult. Moreover, due to the stochasticity of the SDS loss, the original gradient-based density control in 3DGS becomes unstable, leading to blurry results with floating artifacts.

In this paper, we propose HumanGaussian, an efficient yet effective framework that generates high-quality 3D humans with fine-grained geometry and realistic appearance. Our intuition is that 3D Gaussian Splatting is an efficient renderer with periodic Gaussian shrinkage or growing, and such adaptive density control can be naturally guided by intrinsic human structures. The key is to incorporate explicit structural guidance and gradient regularization into Gaussian optimization. Specifically, we first propose a Structure-Aware SDS that jointly learns human appearance and geometry. Unlike previous studies [42,43,36] that adopt generic priors such as Structure-from-Motion (SfM) points or Point-E [44], we anchor the initial Gaussian positions on the SMPL-X mesh. The subsequent densification and pruning thus focus on regions around the body surface, effectively capturing geometric deformations like accessories and wrinkles. We further extend the pre-trained Stable Diffusion [16] to denoise image RGB and depth simultaneously, and use it as our SDS source model. This dual-branch design distills the joint distribution of two spatially-aligned targets (i.e., RGB and depth), boosting Gaussian convergence with both structural guidance and textural realism. To further improve the naturalness of renderings, we devise an Annealed Negative Prompt Guidance. We decompose SDS into a noisier generative score and a cleaner classifier score, and equip the latter with a decreasing negative prompt guidance, which enables realistic generation under nominal CFG scales (e.g., 7.5), as also shown in concurrent text-to-3D studies [45,46]. In this way, we avoid over-saturated patterns with appropriate CFG scales that balance sample quality and diversity. Moreover, because of the high variance of the SDS loss, relying directly on gradient information to control densities leads to blurry geometry [36]. Instead, we eliminate floating artifacts based on Gaussian size in a prune-only phase.

To summarize, our main contributions are three-fold: 1) We propose HumanGaussian, an efficient yet effective framework for high-quality 3D human generation with fine-grained geometry and realistic appearance. As one of the earliest attempts at taming Gaussian Splatting for the text-driven 3D human domain, we hope it paves the way for future research. 2) We propose the Structure-Aware SDS, which jointly learns human appearance and geometry with explicit structural guidance. 3) We devise the Annealed Negative Prompt Guidance to ensure realistic results and eliminate floating artifacts. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior efficiency and competitive quality of our framework, which renders vivid 3D humans in diverse scenarios.
